Projects

In addition to our ongoing funded and independent research projects, we are always interested in listening to new ideas and forming new collaborations, so if nothing that we ware currently doing sounds like what you are interested in, please reach out!

Ongoing research

Ongoing · 2026–present

Multimodal Visualization Authoring

Exploring How Students Design Visualizations with Integrated Sketching, Natural Language, and Code Editing

People: Sadie Fisher, Dr. Austin P. Wright, Dr. Ayaan Kazerouni

Ongoing · 2026–present

Interactive Synthetic Data Tool for User Evaluation of Exploratory Data Analysis Methods

Developing a tool to study how well dimensionality reduction techniques enable effective truth tracking data exploration when given to actual users.

People: Khoa Ly, Greg Phillips, Dr. Austin P. Wright

Ongoing · 2026–present

Interactive Visualization of Bayes Networks

Developing an interactive visualization tool for Probabilistic Graphical Models as an interface towards general purpose probabilistic programing in a visual mode. Ongoing work includes both tool design and development as well as empirical studies to understand the strengths and weaknesses of visual as opposed to code based workflows.

People: Tobin Bohley, Dr. Austin P. Wright

Ongoing · 2026–present

Multimodal and Multiscale Latent Representation of Biodiversity Data

Extending work on the Biocube biodiversity dataset to build multimodal and multi-scale latent representations of complex relational data, and studying ways to interactively build interpretable scientific visualizations on top of the representation.

People: Aiden Freeland, Dr. Austin P. Wright

Ongoing · 2026–present

Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Visual Environment

Reinforcement learning is famously difficult to train, and multi-agent environments doubly so. A key aspect of effective training is visibility in to the emergent patterns and behaviors that agents exhibit in the RL environment. This project is studying ways to gain better real time visibility into the multi-agent RL environment to better enable the rapid identification and analysis of learned behaviours.

People: Pranav Nallaperumal, Dr. Austin P. Wright

Past projects

Past · 2026

Cognitive Effects of AI Authorship labels on Interpretive Domains

An empirical study of how perceptions of AI attribution to analysis affects how people respond to analysis in open interpretive domain of art criticism.

People: Sam Kaplan, Dr. Austin P. Wright
